symbols.name: fixed bilinear space
symbols.meaning: The fixed vector space on which the bilinear form is defined and on which all labels lie.
symbols.quote: Subspace labels are based on the fixed bilinear space $F$, whose [Bilinear form](bilinear-form.md) $\langle p,q\rangle$ is linear in each argument, where $p$ and $q$ are vectors of $F$.

symbols.name: first vector
symbols.meaning: A vector of F, the first argument of the bilinear form.
symbols.quote: Subspace labels are based on the fixed bilinear space $F$, whose [Bilinear form](bilinear-form.md) $\langle p,q\rangle$ is linear in each argument, where $p$ and $q$ are vectors of $F$.

symbols.name: second vector
symbols.meaning: A vector of F, the second argument of the bilinear form.
symbols.quote: Subspace labels are based on the fixed bilinear space $F$, whose [Bilinear form](bilinear-form.md) $\langle p,q\rangle$ is linear in each argument, where $p$ and $q$ are vectors of $F$.

symbols.name: smaller label
symbols.meaning: A nondegenerate subspace of F attached to a wire; on an edge, the label contained in the other.
symbols.quote: A label $L$ is a nondegenerate subspace of $F$, meaning $L\cap L^{\perp}=\{0\}$, where $L^{\perp}$ is the set of vectors orthogonal to every vector of $L$.

symbols.name: larger label
symbols.meaning: On an edge, the label that contains the smaller label L.
symbols.quote: For an edge with $L\subseteq M$, $L$ and $M$ are its smaller and larger label.

symbols.name: orthogonal residual
symbols.meaning: On an edge, the subspace of the larger label M orthogonal to the smaller label L.
symbols.quote: Its orthogonal residual is $R=M\cap L^{\perp}$, the orthogonal complement of the smaller label inside the larger one.

symbols.name: component in L
symbols.meaning: The part of a vector p in M that lies in the smaller label L.
symbols.quote: For $p\in M$, write $p=c+r$ with $c\in L$ and $r\in L^{\perp}$; then $r=p-c\in M$, so $r\in R$.

symbols.name: component in residual
symbols.meaning: The part of a vector p in M that lies in L^perp, and hence in the residual R.
symbols.quote: For $p\in M$, write $p=c+r$ with $c\in L$ and $r\in L^{\perp}$; then $r=p-c\in M$, so $r\in R$.
